_comment: Field truth: marks of standing that Thai people already recognise, which no global platform carries. Two kinds. (1) royal — พระอารามหลวง, the ecclesiastical grade a temple holds, class (ชั้นเอก/โท/ตรี) and kind (ราชวรมหาวิหาร…สามัญ). This is a real hierarchy, not a ranking we invented. (2) food — เครื่องหมายรับรอง that diners here actually trust. Every entry carries the year of the edition it was read from and the URL it was read on, because these lists change yearly and a dated mark is true forever while an undated one rots. Nothing goes in the verified lists without a fetched source. Never let an importer or crawl write this file.

_food_comment: Chiang Rai province is not covered by the MICHELIN Guide Thailand at all, so an empty Chiang Rai list is the answer rather than a gap. Chiang Mai had no starred restaurants in the 2026 edition. The michelin.com listing pages render client-side and could not be read; the only michelin.com page that gave distinctions is an article dated 20 July 2022, so those entries carry edition 2022 and the badge says so. Entries read from the current listing without a visible distinction are recorded as michelin-guide — in the guide, distinction unread.
